description: Square four-post canopy module roofed in split bamboo culms laid alternately hollow-up and hollow-down as interlocking tiles, low gabled, open on all sides.

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: Square four-post canopy module with a low gabled roof of split bamboo culms laid alternately hollow-up and hollow-down as interlocking tiles, whole bamboo posts at the four corners lashed to a bamboo beam frame, open on all sides Materials: Split bamboo culms weathered from green through straw to grey, nodes and longitudinal fibre splits showing, dark rot and insect holes at the cut ends, natural fibre rope lashings blackened at the joints.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93. 3,480/4,000 triangles, 4/4 draw calls, 3/3 materials, 4/6 unique geometries, two 512 px and one 256 px canvas. Open on all four sides and the eave is 17 open culm mouths: turntable with --allow-holes, holeviz read per azimuth showing the red over the gable voids and the volume between posts and rails only.

featureReviews.evidence: Envelope measured 3.940 x 3.100 x 3.980 m off the built module: the roof owns +-1.970 / +-1.990, the frame stops at +-1.95, and the four 160 mm posts at +-1.68 sit 0.23 m inside the eave -- the plate's overhang of about one post diameter. Double head rail at 2.03 and 2.27 with its ends running 0.19 m past the posts, as the plate shows at every corner. Capping culm crown exactly 3.100. Open on all four sides.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's pitch is nearer 25 degrees; the notes' 2.40 / 3.10 with the overhang gives 15.6 and is the module contract. Posts flush with the eave were the first build's largest departure from the plate.

featureReviews.evidence: 17 hollow-up channels (r 0.085) on a 233 mm pitch and 16 hollow-down caps (r 0.120) bridging their rims, ten segments each, as TWO instanced sets so every culm carries its own tone: green / cream / grey strips in no order, caps independent of channels, measured back at 185 (cream) and ~150 (green) on the hero slope against the plate's 197 / 150-160. The eave is 17 open mouths and reads as the plate's scallop at 0 and 180; the split tile puts a node ring, fibre grain, a drying split and rot holes with stained halos on every culm.
featureReviews.notes: The first build's 33 pairs at 118 mm read as a stripey mat; the plate's eave shows 13-15 scallops across the bay. One pair geometry also forced each cap to share its channel's tone.

featureReviews.evidence: Culm tones probed and re-authored on this build: posts measured back at 118 and rails at 127 on the hero, 122 on the back-lit 180 frame, against the plate's 107-120 (the first build rendered 161 at the same pixels). Forty rope collars on a third material with a laid-strand tile: post-head wraps spanning both rails, whippings on all sixteen rail ends, ten rafter feet, the ridge and king culms, black cord below -- rope measured 134 against the plate's 130, cord held on chroma at luma 67 / sat 0.49. Node rings at 0.60 m on every pole whichever way it is turned.
featureReviews.notes: The lashings are collars with strand relief in the tile, not modelled X-wraps; the X of a square lashing is under a centimetre of relief at prop distance.

name: Bamboo Half-Pipe Canopy Module
nameTh: หลังคาไม้ไผ่ผ่าซีก
notes: One bay of a modular outdoor roof kit: 4 x 4 m footprint on a 4 m grid, which divides the kit's 8 m ground and road tiles exactly 2 x 2, so a canopy grid lands on the paving grid. Four corner posts, because the brief is a module that includes its own poles and must therefore stand alone; placed side by side the posts pair up at the shared edges, which is what a real market row looks like rather than a defect to design out. Gabled with the ridge across the module, eave 2.4 m and ridge 3.1 m. Open on all sides. The alternating half-pipe course is the identity of this roof and is the one place in the set where the roof surface may need real geometry rather than a normal map -- a run of half-cylinders reads wrong when it is flat, because the silhouette at the eave is a scalloped edge and not a line. Build the scallop into the eave edge at minimum, and expect this module to sit nearer its triangle ceiling than the others in the set.
